title: Serve the first slice from a full pie pan
instruction: Use the pie server to lift the first slice of the cut pumpkin pie from the near side of the pan. Serve the whole slice upright on the dessert plate and draw the server clear. Keep both grippers off the food.
context: At a family meal the first slice has neighbours on both sides. The server must pass over the intact rim and beneath the bottom crust, support the filling across the gap, and emerge after the plate takes the slice.
setup: Use a chilled, firmly set pumpkin pie cut into eight equal 45-degree slices. All eight remain in a standard 9-inch-inside aluminum pan, with its full sloped 19 mm lip and 257 mm outer flange. The target wedge faces the operator. The nominal knife gaps are 2.5 mm. Each of the seven other slices rests freely. The empty 91 x 48 mm tapered offset server starts on the bench with the point outside the pan and the wooden handle on a short rest. The 170 mm plate is 245 mm to the right and 12 mm forward of the pan centre. See README for the fixed reset measurements.
scoring: Earn 0.25 when the target slice rests on the server with the whole bottom crust at least 5 mm above the pan lip for a quarter second. The crust and filling must stay upright within 15 degrees, with the point and both outside corners of the filling within 9 mm of their matching crust positions. Earn 0.5 after the server carries the aligned slice fully past the plate-side edge of the pan by 5 mm for half a second. Lower the slice until the plate and server briefly support it together. Earn 0.75 when the whole slice then rests inside the plate edge, bottom-crust down within 7 degrees and still aligned, for a quarter second. Earn 1 when the entire blade clears both layers by at least 5 mm and that plated finish holds for the final second. Any gripper touching the target food voids the trial. Use overhead and level side views with a ruler. After handoff, the underside rests flush on the plate. Inspect the point, heel and corners for daylight. A missing layer or displaced tip fails the integrity check.
fidelity: The complete metal pan, sloping outer pastry and tapered server are physical colliders. All eight cut portions rest freely. The target has two moveable layers. The bottom and curved outer pastry form one piece, while the filling can tip, fall or slide out of its shell. This approximates firmly set chilled pie. Internal cracks, crumbs, adhesion and local bending of pastry or server are outside this simulation. Friction is estimated.
reset_notes: Place all eight cut portions back in the pan on their bottoms with the near portion centred toward the operator. Remove the cutting guide completely. Set the empty server outside the pan and return the stock jaws to their open home pose.
